verdict.rationale: Replicate documents a large catalog of community-published open-source models, runnable with one line of code. Public models are billed only for processing time and scale automatically, including down to zero, which fits shared serverless endpoints. However, the evidence never names the specific open-weight LLM families in the story, and the examples shown are mostly image models. Missing for 10: explicit evidence that Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek or GPT-OSS models are in the catalog, confirmation that current LLM families are kept up to date, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can choose among a broad catalog of current open-weight model families (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, GPT-OSS and peers) on shared serverless endpoints

citations.quote: Our community has already published thousands of models that are ready to use in production. You can run these with one line of code.
Thousands of open-source machine learning models have been contributed by our community and more are added every day.
When running or training one of these public models, you only pay for the time it takes to process your request.
If you don't get any traffic, we scale down to zero and don't charge you a thing.
